issues.description: The code requires multiple named local and CSMAR/Wind inputs, plus two dynamic People’s Daily workbook corpora. The package inventory contains a verified prepared Qing Jinshi workbook and a separate six-field DTA, but the latter is not read by supplied code and is not a complete panel. The exact compatible routes, People’s Daily annual files/fields/coverage, and some input-to-output contracts remain unresolved; catalog misses are not evidence of absent licenses or access barriers.

Files 01–10 set path to an empty string and point rawdata/data/output at ${path}/Data; on POSIX the literal expands to [redacted-path-1cd22566382a]. Those files do not set a project root or change cwd. The two People’s Daily variants use backslash paths and distinct Data/Output roots. Configure host-visible, consistent roots in a separate working copy.
File 06’s active dividend import line opens the CSV filename quote and does not close it. A one-character closing-quote edit preserves the same target and import operation in a working copy.

File 08’s active `gen ret = R-Rm /` expression ends with a division operator and no operand; the next line is blank and then the save command, with no comment or continuation supplying a term. The return.dta producer is therefore blocked by malformed source text. The intended numerator/denominator/formula is not supplied and must not be guessed.

evidence.file: GSZ datasheet.pdf
evidence.quote:
(g) Hand-collected data:
      i.   The number of Jinshi in the Qing Dynasty, processed in November 2019.
           The primary data source is A list of jinshi in Qing Dynasty, which collects demo-
           graphic information about all Jinshi in the Qing Dynasty (e.g., name, the ranking
           in the corresponding court exam, hometown, etc.). From this source, we identify the
           hometowns of 25,449 Jinshi out of a population of 26,748 individuals. We collect the
           hometowns of 286 additional Jinshi from The Draft History of Qing, A List of Im-
           perial Clan Jinshi in Qing Dynasty, The Collection of Keju Examination Papers in
           Qing Dynasty, and General History of Fengtian, giving us data on the hometowns of
           25,735 Jinshi or 96% of the total Jinshi population in the Qing Dynasty.
evidence.description: The datasheet describes the author’s prepared Qing Jinshi input and reports its historical coverage.
